comparison: Both evaluate human ACD tissue validation (C72-C78). OpenEval finds claims supported with note of limited sample size. Peer reviewers express uncertainty: Reviewer 1 notes indirect co-localization evidence, Reviewer 3 finds IF data unconvincing and inconsistent with targets.

Both address background/introductory claims (C1-C7 in OpenEval, C1-C10 in peer). OpenEval finds these well-supported by literature. Peer reviewers note no challenges to these established contextual facts.
OpenEval R2 addresses rationale claims (C8-C10) with partial overlap to peer R10. Both find these background claims supported by appropriate citations without controversy.

Both evaluate ACD model characterization (C11-C14 in OpenEval, C11-C12 in peer). OpenEval finds model well-documented with appropriate data. Peer reviewers describe manuscript as comprehensive with no challenges to model characterization.

Both address cytokine source identification (C15-C18). OpenEval highlights basophils as IL4/IL13 source challenging conventional understanding. Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly confirms the study deconvolved cytokine sources including IL4/13 from basophils, describing analyses as well-presented.

Both evaluate T cell characterization (C19-C23 in OpenEval, C19-C31 in peer). OpenEval supports central memory T cell findings. Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly confirms type 1 inflammatory response findings and describes analyses as well-presented and thoughtful.

Both address type-1 T cell polarization (C24-C31). OpenEval finds strong convergent evidence from multiple approaches. Peer reviewers explicitly confirm type 1 inflammatory response centered on IFNG from CD4/CD8 T cells, with editor describing data as convincing.

Both evaluate basophil and myeloid cell characterization (C32-C47). OpenEval supports detailed characterization of type-2 cytokine sources. Peer Reviewer 1 confirms deconvolution of cytokine sources including IL4/13 from basophils and IL1B from neutrophils/macrophages.

Both address myeloid cell activation (C41-C47 in OpenEval, overlapping with R3 peer claims). OpenEval finds coordinated myeloid activation with IFNγ as key regulator. Peer reviewers confirm these findings as well-presented without challenges.

Both evaluate IFNγ-responsive preadipocyte/fibroblast identification (C48-C52 in OpenEval, C48-C56 in peer). OpenEval supports this key finding with multiple analytical approaches. Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly confirms identification of dermal fibroblast subpopulation upregulating CXCL9/10, with editor describing data as convincing.

Both address chemokine co-localization with fibroblasts (C53-C56). OpenEval finds co-immunostaining validates scRNA-seq findings. Peer reviewers describe data as convincing, though Reviewer 3 separately critiques IF quality in R8.

Peer R8 specifically critiques IF data quality for C53 (and C77), finding staining unconvincing and inconsistent. OpenEval R10 supports these claims based on co-localization data. This represents a methodological quality disagreement.

Both address vitiligo comparison (C57-C59 in OpenEval, C57-C58 in peer R4). OpenEval supports similarity suggesting conserved mechanisms. Peer reviewers note this comparison as part of convincing overall findings.
OpenEval R11 includes C59 on vitiligo similarity. Peer R5 addresses in vitro validation (C59-C68). Both find these claims supported, with peer reviewers describing conclusions as well-supported.

Both evaluate in vitro fibroblast stimulation experiments (C60-C63). OpenEval finds RNA-seq and time-course data validate in vivo findings. Peer Reviewer 1 confirms in vitro experiments demonstrate CXCL9/10 expression by IFNγ-stimulated fibroblasts as part of well-presented manuscript.

Both address co-culture and CXCR3 blocking experiments (C64-C68). OpenEval finds functional validation demonstrates fibroblast-T cell axis through CXCR3. Peer reviewers describe these in vitro experiments as well-presented with conclusions well-supported.

Both evaluate Ifngr1 knockout experiments (C69-C71, plus C86-C88 in peer). OpenEval finds strong causal evidence for dFB-T cell axis. Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly confirms genetic evidence demonstrates important role for IFNγ signaling in fibroblasts, with editor describing data as convincing.

OpenEval R16 addresses main conclusion (C79) finding it supported by convergent multi-level evidence. Peer R11 addresses discussion claims including C79, treating overall conclusions as reasonable contextualization.

Both address abstract summary claims. OpenEval R17 covers C80-C88, finding them consistent with evidence. Peer R1 confirms key findings including cytokine source deconvolution (C80-C83), describing data as convincing.
OpenEval R17 includes C84 on fibroblast subpopulation identification. Peer R4 addresses overlapping claims about dermal fibroblasts, with reviewers finding data convincing.
OpenEval R17 includes C85 on in vitro validation. Peer R5 addresses in vitro experiments (C59-C68, C85), finding them well-presented and conclusions well-supported.
OpenEval R17 includes C86-C88 on genetic validation. Peer R6 addresses same knockout claims (C69-C71, C86-C88), with explicit confirmation of genetic evidence and convincing data.

Both address discussion/context claims. OpenEval R18 covers C89-C93 on prior literature context, finding appropriate citations. Peer R11 addresses broader discussion (C79, C89-C103), noting thoughtful discussion of limitations and comparisons.
Both address vitiligo study citations (C94-C96). OpenEval finds accurate citation of parallel findings. Peer reviewers note authors compared data to vitiligo model to demonstrate similar mechanisms.
Both address IFNGR signaling complexity discussion (C97-C98). OpenEval finds appropriate acknowledgment of context-dependent effects. Peer reviewers treat discussion as reasonable contextualization.
Both address model-specific differences discussion (C99-C100). OpenEval finds appropriate contextualization of findings. Peer reviewers note thoughtful discussion of study limitations.
Both address basophil biology citations (C101). OpenEval finds appropriate context provided. Peer reviewers treat discussion claims as reasonable without specific challenges.

Both address speculative therapeutic implications (C102-C103). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting C103 is explicitly speculative without direct support but appropriately presented as hypothesis. Peer reviewers treat discussion as reasonable contextualization without flagging speculation as problematic.
